sources.title: Huawei OD interview source note containing the raw 'two numbers multiply' wording
Structured repository question normalized as big integer multiplication
LeetCode official articles index containing 43. Multiply Strings
43 - Multiply Strings problem mirror and grade-school multiplication solution

claims.text: The raw interview note only says the coding problem was 'two numbers multiply'; the repository's later structured question adds the big-integer interpretation. The candidate therefore labels LeetCode-43-style decimal-string multiplication as a practice contract rather than attributing the full contract to the raw note.

LeetCode 43 models multiplication of two non-negative integers represented as decimal strings, returns the product as a string, and forbids using a built-in BigInteger implementation or converting the whole inputs directly to integers; the standard examples include 2*3 -> 6 and 123*456 -> 56088.

For m- and n-digit decimal inputs, the product has at most m+n digits. Accumulating each digit pair into position i+j+1 and then propagating carries from right to left implements grade-school multiplication without converting the entire inputs to machine integers.
The implementation examines every pair of input digits once and uses an m+n accumulation array, so runtime is O(m*n) and auxiliary space is O(m+n).

The exact Java implementation passes two standard examples, zero and carry-heavy boundaries, repository-local leading-zero normalization, invalid-input checks, and 5000 deterministic random decimal pairs up to 80 digits compared against java.math.BigInteger used only as an independent test oracle.

findings: The raw source note is materially less specific than the normalized Canonical, so the candidate correctly treats decimal-string big-integer multiplication as a practice mapping rather than fabricated source detail.

The LeetCode-43-style contract matches the repository's normalized 'big integer multiplication' intent and is a standard meaningful hand-coding task where ordinary integer multiplication would be trivial.
The m+n digit-capacity and i+j+1 accumulation invariant are mathematically sound and are explained rather than merely asserted.
The exact Java implementation does not use BigInteger or whole-input numeric conversion; BigInteger appears only in the independent test oracle.
The implementation passes targeted boundary cases and 5000 deterministic differential cases; no code placeholder or cross-question reuse remains in the candidate.
Leading-zero handling is explicitly labeled as a repository-local defensive extension rather than part of the official LeetCode input contract.
No personal or production experience is fabricated. Human approval remains a separate promotion gate under the current batch policy.
